jobs.title: System Software Engineer – Data Center GPU Compute Diagnostics
jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

  

We are seeking a system software engineer to develop low-level diagnostic software for next-generation data center GPUs and rack-scale AI systems. Our team builds software that exercises and validates complex hardware, including compute engines, memory and cache subsystems, NICs, PCIe and NVLink interfaces, power delivery, and thermal behavior. This role is well suited to an embedded, firmware, device-driver, hardware-validation, or systems software engineer who enjoys working close to hardware. Relevant experience may come from GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage, servers, embedded systems, or other complex silicon-based products. Prior GPU, CUDA, or GEMM experience is helpful but not required; you will have the opportunity to learn GPU architecture and programming while working with experienced engineers. You will own well-scoped components of the diagnostic software from design through implementation, validation, productization, and field support. You will collaborate with hardware architects, driver developers, silicon-validation engineers, manufacturing teams, and field engineers to bring up new hardware and diagnose difficult system failures. Join an exciting, rewarding, and fast-moving environment building the systems that power modern AI.

  

**What you’ll be doing:**

* Developing diagnostic and stress software in C/C++ and Python for complex hardware systems.
* Interfacing with hardware blocks, firmware, Linux device drivers, registers, telemetry, and low-level debugging tools.
* Bringing up and validating new silicon and system features using pre-production hardware and software.
* Creating targeted tests for compute engines, memory and cache subsystems, DMA engines, PCIe/NVLink interfaces, power, and thermal behavior.
* Investigating hardware and software failures involving memory errors, ECC, data integrity, performance, thermals, voltage/frequency behavior, and high-speed interfaces.
* Contributing to diagnostic and stress workloads ranging from low-level tests for GPU hardware to higher-level AI workloads, with opportunities to develop expertise in CUDA programming, GEMM-style compute, NCCL, and PyTorch-based workloads.
Using modern development and analysis tools, including AI-assisted tools where appropriate, to accelerate coding, debugging, test creation, and failure analysis.  

  

**What we need to see:**

* BS or MS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 2+ years of experience in embedded software, firmware, Linux device drivers, systems software, hardware validation, diagnostics, or silicon bring-up.
* Strong programming skills in C and C++, plus working proficiency in Python.
* Experience developing software that interacts with hardware, firmware, device drivers, hardware registers, or low-level interfaces.
* Experience creating diagnostics, validation tests, stress tests, manufacturing tests, or other software used to isolate hardware or system failures.
* Understanding of fundamental computer architecture concepts such as memory, caches, interrupts, DMA, buses, and device I/O.
* Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate failures across hardware and software boundaries.
* Ability to take ownership of a well-scoped problem and drive it to completion while collaborating with a technical lead and cross-functional teams.
Good written and verbal communication skills.  

  

Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 124,000 USD - 195,500 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits .

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 25, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes.

NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Front-End (UI) Platform Engineer-Retail Point of Sale Systems
jobs.description:
**Note:** Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions will not be providing visa sponsorship for this position now or in the future. Therefore, in order to be considered for this position, **you must have the ability to work in the United States without a need for current or future visa sponsorship**.

* **Must be local to Raleigh/Durham, NC Area or Bentonville, AR Area. This is a hybrid role at least 3 days a week in person.**

Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions is seeking a Front-End (UI) Platform Engineer-Retail Point of Sale Systems to own and evolve the ELERA point-of-sale client – the Vue 3 and TypeScript application framework behind our fixed-lane, self-checkout, kiosk, specialty, associate-mobile, and customer-display experiences. This is a successor role on a defined architect track: the person hired will be trained to become the architect for the ELERA POS client.

This is a platform role, not a feature role. Most of the work is not screens. It is the framework other teams build their screens out of: a dependency-injection and plugin system that retailers and partners extend through, a configuration merge chain that resolves customer overrides, a device layer that talks to lane hardware, a legacy Dojo application that must keep shipping beside the modern client, and the build train that releases all of it together.

The role requires experience building solutions on Vue.js and Java enterprise technologies with a focus on complex browser-side functionality. The ideal candidate will excel in our fast-paced, collaborative, customer-first environment, and is looking for a path into architecture rather than a larger backlog.

**Responsibilities:**

* Design, develop, and test/debug client UI and client framework code in Vue 3 and TypeScript, and mentor the team doing the same

* Design with other developers in mind – both the internal team and the retailer, partner, and services engineers who extend the platform from outside

* Own and extend the client extensibility model: dependency injection and decorator-based registration, plugin loading, UI slot injection, and the base/TGCS/partner/customer configuration merge chain

* Maintain backward compatibility for plugins and customizations built against earlier framework versions

* Publish versioned shared packages consumed by other teams, with real semantic-versioning and deprecation discipline

* Keep two UI generations shippable at once, migrating the legacy Dojo layer incrementally rather than by flag day

* Extend the device integration layer – scanners, scales, printers, payment terminals, cash recyclers, customer display – including the mock device harness that lets the full client run on a laptop

* Maintain the client release train: hybrid Maven/npm builds, monorepo publishing, Jenkins multi-branch pipelines across the framework dependency chain, and constrained or air-gapped customer environments

* Own client-side quality: unit and component tests under a coverage gate, and a browser-automated BDD suite that gates the build

* Write and defend architecture decision records, component analyses, and solution designs; represent the client stack at the Architecture Review Board

* Maintain the client Self-Enablement Guide and generated extension catalogs, and serve as a technical interface to key technology partners

* Perform unit and functional tests of product features, and resolve unit, functional, and customer- or partner-reported defects across supported release lines

* Provide reasonable estimates, meet deliverables while assisting the team, and enable the team to meet their KPIs

* Use good programming patterns, call out anti-patterns, and handle accelerating change in pursuit of more innovative solutions

**Required Skills:**

* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent experience

* Software Engineer III: 5+ years of professional web development experience. Software Engineer IV: 9+ years of full-stack web development experience, particularly client side

* Strong analytical and TypeScript/OO programming skills, including generics, declaration files, and strict-mode discipline

* 2+ years in Vue 3 or an equivalent modern component framework, at depth: reactivity semantics, routing, and centralized state management

* Experience building shared libraries or frameworks that other teams consume – not only end-user features

* Working knowledge of a dependency-injection / inversion-of-control container (InversifyJS, tsyringe, Angular DI, Spring, or similar) and decorator-based registration; understanding of lifetimes and resolution order

* Deep technical skills in web development technologies (HTML5, JavaScript, TypeScript, SASS, XML/JSON, Vue.js), including module-system fluency (ESM, AMD, UMD) and modern build tooling such as Vite

* Unit testing as a default habit, plus browser automation with at least one of Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium – including the ability to diagnose a flaky test rather than retry it

* Demonstrated ability to work productively inside a large legacy code base without rewriting it

* Experience developing in a Java-based environment, including enterprise/web-based content, sufficient to debug a service you do not own and determine where a defect actually lives

* REST and OpenAPI contract thinking, including a working definition of a breaking change

* Comfort in CI/CD: pipelines, containerized builds, artifact registries, dependency resolution, lockfiles, and transitive version conflicts

* Proficiency with Git at team scale: long-lived release lines, backports, and conflict resolution that does not lose work

* Experience with operating systems – Linux, Windows, iOS or Android; installation, light administration, and simple scripting

* Knowledge of software development concepts, methodology, and life cycle, especially Agile

* Clear technical writing, and a record of documenting decisions that others then followed. Communication is a hiring criterion for this role, not a bonus

* Strong pro

jobs.title: Cryogenic Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
**Full-time | On-site in the Research Triangle area, North Carolina | Reports to the Scientific and Technical Director**

LH3M is developing a cryopump and sorption collector for lunar gases. Initial work uses small loads of standard helium, predominantly He-4, followed by controlled mixed-gas experiments. We seek an engineer or experimental physicist with substantial hands-on experience designing, commissioning and troubleshooting low-temperature apparatus.

You will own the collector’s cryogenic and thermal performance. Evaluate commercial cryopumps and refrigeration hardware, develop cold surfaces and sorbent assemblies, and determine how collected gas can be retained and recovered through controlled regeneration.

**Responsibilities**

* Assess commercial cryopump suitability, required operating temperatures, cooling capacity, access and modification constraints.
* Develop thermal budgets, shielding, supports, thermal interfaces, temperature sensing and control with the systems engineer.
* Evaluate staged capture of water, nitrogen and oxygen while measuring helium transmission, retention and losses.
* Design and conduct tests of capture efficiency, sorption capacity, breakthrough, regeneration and recovery over repeated cycles.
* Commission cold and vacuum systems, diagnose performance limits, and establish documented operating and safety procedures.

**Required experience**

* Degree in mechanical engineering, physics, applied physics or a related field, or equivalent specialist experience.
* Demonstrated personal responsibility for helium-temperature cryogenic apparatus, including cooldowns, thermometry, thermal troubleshooting and vacuum operation.
* Working knowledge of conduction and radiation heat loads, vacuum practices, leak detection and gas handling.
* Ability to design quantitative experiments, assess uncertainty and explain results clearly. Relevant industrial and research experience are both welcome.

**Preferred experience**

Cryopumps, adsorption or sorption, cryocoolers, cold traps, residual gas analysis, and gas inventory measurements. Experience modifying commercial equipment is especially valuable. A PhD is welcome but not required.

**What success looks like**

A defensible cold-system design and repeatable measurements showing where helium goes during capture, retention and regeneration, with thermal limits and losses understood.

*Provide a résumé and describe a cryogenic system you personally commissioned or modified, including a performance problem you diagnosed.*

Pay: $125,000.00 - $155,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

jobs.description:
**Software Engineer, Race Operations Systems**
==============================================

**Richard Childress Racing | Welcome, North Carolina | Full time** **Reports to the Director of Development and Innovation**

**The job**
-----------

Every Sunday a Cup race is decided by information. You build the software that moves that information: the pipelines that pull data off the car, out of the simulation, and in from the sanctioning body, and the internal apps our engineers open on a race weekend. The ideal candidate will have development experience, with a strong background in system architecture, and competency across the full stack.

You inherit a working set of applications, you own them, and you decide what gets built next. You report straight to the Director of Development and Innovation and you will have a direct line to the people setting the technical direction of the race team.

**What you will do**
--------------------

* Own the full lifecycle of our internal applications: design, build, deploy, maintain, retire. Some of it alone, some with a small team.
* Build and maintain the data pipelines that collect, clean, and stage data for automated analysis.
* Create high-performing applications within the bounds of external constraints, seeking creative and efficient solutions to problems.
* Ship full-stack internal tools that engineers use on a race weekend, which means they have to be fast, right, and ready by Friday.
* Run CI/CD and source control. Git, automated tests, repeatable deployments.
* Research and recommend software, and sometimes hardware to achieve project goals
* Carry several projects at once and tell people plainly what is shipping and when.
* BS in Computer Science
* At least 3 years building software, backend preferred.

**What we need**
----------------

* Ability to design complex systems at scale
* Strong with REST APIs, SQL, and S3-style object storage.
* Python required. Rust or C# a plus. Comfortable with a variety of languages
* Experience with React or an equivalent frontend framework, along with a basic understanding of UI and HCI concepts
* Data and plotting libraries: polars, matplotlib, plotly, d3, or their equivalents.
* Experience with Git version control
* Attention to detail.
* Self-starter who can shape key design decisions through research and analysis
* Strong verbal and written communication of complex systems
* Desire to work in a fast-paced, quality-driven, collaborative environment
* Microsoft Azure experience is a plus.

**A plus**
----------

Prior work in NASCAR, IndyCar, Formula 1, or another professional motorsports organization.

**Why now**
-----------

RCR has created a Development and Innovation group to change how the race team uses data and software. The person in this seat builds the foundation that group runs on. If you want your code to show up in a race result, this is the job.

You should be proficient in:

* Professional motorsports
* REST APIs
* S-3-style object storage
* Software building experience
* SQL
* Python

Machines & technologies you'll use:

* Microsoft Azure
* Plotly
* Polars
* Matplotlib

jobs.description:

**Company:** Corning

  

Requisition Number: 79264

  

**The company built on breakthroughs.**  
**Join us.**

Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible.

How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward.

At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.

Come break through with us.

The carrier network product group consists primarily of products and solutions for optical-based communications infrastructure for services such as video, data and voice communications. jobs.title: Junior IoT Engineer
jobs.description:
Note

* Hybrid, may be asked to come into the office for hands-on tasks

Junior IoT Engineer

**No engineering degree required, but curiosity is.**

We're a small IoT company building and deploying real-world sensor systems, and we're looking for someone early in their engineering career who loves learning how things work.

You might be getting an Electrical Engineering or Computer Science degree. You might have gone to trade school. You might be self-taught and have a desk covered in Arduinos, Raspberry Pis, wires, and half-finished projects.

We're interested in what you can **do and learn**, not the name on your diploma.

Show us what you've built

Seriously.

Built something with an Arduino? Designed a PCB? Made a robot? Automated your house? Written firmware? Set up a home server? Repaired electronics? Built something completely ridiculous just because you wanted to see if you could?

**Tell us about it.**

Personal projects, hobbies, and things you've taught yourself matter to us.

What you'll do

You'll work with real IoT hardware throughout its entire lifecycle—from engineering prototypes to devices deployed in the field.

Your work will include:

* Configuring and preparing IoT devices for deployment
* Managing firmware and device settings across our fleet
* Testing and QA'ing sensors before they become finished goods
* Troubleshooting devices that don't behave the way they're supposed to
* Using fleet data to investigate problems and identify trends
* Testing new hardware and firmware designs
* Presenting feedback to the rest of the R&D team
* Learning to diagnose PCB, sensor, power, firmware, and RF problems
* Helping us improve the tools and processes we use to configure, test, and deploy devices

Some days you'll be working with production hardware. Other days you might be looking through logs, testing a prototype, chasing down an RF problem, writing a script to automate something annoying, or putting an oscilloscope on a board to figure out what went wrong.

That's part of the fun.

Things you'll learn

We **do not expect you to already know all of these.**

Experience with any of them is a bonus. More importantly, we're looking for someone **excited to learn**:

* Microcontrollers and embedded systems
* Linux and the command line
* Firmware and device management
* PCB debugging
* Sensors and IoT systems
* RF and wireless communications
* Data analysis and troubleshooting
* Python and scripting
* Electronics test equipment, including:
* Multimeters
* Oscilloscopes
* Logic analyzers
* Programmable power supplies and loads
* Other lab equipment you'll probably find an excuse to play with

You'll get exposure to the full lifecycle of an IoT product:

**prototype → hardware → firmware → testing → production → deployment → fleet data → field troubleshooting**

Who we're looking for

We're looking for someone who is:

* Curious
* Hands-on
* Comfortable saying, "I don't know, but I can figure it out"
* Excited to learn new tools
* Willing to dig into weird problems
* Careful enough to do good production and QA work
* Interested in understanding *why* something failed instead of simply replacing it
* Happy working across hardware, software, data, and production rather than staying in one narrow lane

If you've ever spent an evening trying to figure out why an Arduino wasn't doing what you told it to do, taken apart an electronic device just to see what was inside, or taught yourself something because you couldn't stop wondering how it worked, you may be exactly who we're looking for.

What it's like working here

You'll report directly to our **Head of Research & Engineering**.

We don't expect a junior engineer to walk through the door already knowing everything. Teaching and mentorship are a major part of how our R&D team operates. You'll start with problems you can tackle and take on increasingly difficult ones as your skills grow.

Because we're a small company, you won't be isolated from the rest of the product. You'll work alongside the people designing, programming, testing, deploying, and supporting the systems you're working on.

That means you'll get exposure to a lot of engineering very quickly.

We're also a team that genuinely enjoys working together. We take the engineering seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. Expect bad puns, plenty of joking around, people jumping in to help each other debug problems, and coworkers who actually enjoy hanging out together.

You do NOT need

* An engineering degree
* Years of professional experience
* To know every tool or technology listed above
* To pretend you know something when you don't

Bring curiosity, a willingness to learn, and something cool you've worked on.

**We can teach a lot of the rest.**

Pay: $20.00 - $30.00 per hour

Expected hours: 30.0 per week

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Cincinnati, OH 45202

jobs.title: Data Center Controls Engineer, Controls Deployment Service
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.
  
  
This position requires access to information that is subject to U.S. export control regulations, and applicants must be a 'U.S. Person' as defined by applicable law, which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.  
  
Key job responsibilities

Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.
  
  
Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
  
  
Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.
  
  
Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers.
  
  
Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders’ management.
  
  
Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.
  
  
Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.
  
  
Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
  
  
Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
  
  
Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.

The problems you solve are technical: modifying controls logic to address operational issues, developing Methods of Procedure (MOPs) for firmware upgrades, or investigating complex alarm discrepancies across monitoring systems. For new builds, you own the controls scope from vendor submittal review through commissioning and turnover. You manage vendor relationships, budgets, and schedules for both service contracts and capital projects. Your internal stakeholders include your Controls Manager, Controls Technicians you provide technical direction to, and partner teams (Construction, Critical Projects Implementation, Commissioning, DCEO).
  
  
About the team  
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
  
  
Why AWS
  
  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

The role focuses on reducing equipment downtime, improving equipment reliability, troubleshooting complex control-system issues, supporting preventive and predictive maintenance activities, and implementing equipment and controls improvements that support safe, efficient, and consistent manufacturing operations.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

* Troubleshoot and resolve complex electrical, controls, automation, and equipment-related failures on manufacturing equipment.
* Diagnose PLC, HMI, servo, variable-frequency drive (VFD), sensor, communication, safety-circuit, and industrial control-system issues.
* Provide technical support to Maintenance Technicians during equipment breakdowns and recurring equipment problems.
* Analyze equipment failures and chronic downtime issues to identify root causes and implement permanent corrective actions.
* Develop, modify, troubleshoot, and maintain PLC and HMI programs as required.
* Support industrial robots and automated material-handling systems, including troubleshooting programming, communication, interlock, and peripheral-equipment issues.
* Maintain backups and appropriate documentation for PLC programs, HMI applications, drive parameters, robot programs, and other critical controls configurations.
* Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, cycle time, uptime, maintainability, and overall manufacturing performance.
* Support equipment installations, upgrades, retrofits, commissioning, and production launches.
* Assist in establishing preventive and predictive maintenance requirements for electrical and controls systems.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to improve recurring equipment problems and reduce unplanned downtime.
* Develop and update electrical drawings, controls documentation, troubleshooting guides, and equipment technical documentation.
* Provide technical training and coaching to Maintenance Technicians on controls, electrical troubleshooting, and automation systems.
* Work with equipment manufacturers, integrators, and outside contractors to resolve technical equipment issues and complete improvement projects.
* Support spare-parts identification and critical controls-component standardization.
* Ensure equipment modifications maintain appropriate machine-safety functionality, including guarding, safety circuits, interlocks, emergency stops, and related controls.
* Follow applicable company safety procedures and electrical-safety requirements during troubleshooting and maintenance activities.
* Participate in continuous improvement, root cause analysis, and equipment reliability initiatives.
* Perform additional duties and projects as assigned.

Qualifications (Preferred):

* 2+ years of experience in industrial controls, automation, equipment engineering, or manufacturing maintenance preferred.
* Experience troubleshooting automated manufacturing equipment in a high-volume production environment strongly preferred.
* Experience supporting equipment reliability and reducing recurring downtime preferred.
* Automotive, die-casting, machining, assembly, or similar manufacturing experience is beneficial

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.

• Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. • Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.  

* Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.
* Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
* Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.

• Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers. • Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholder’s management.  

* Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.
* Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.
* Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
* Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
* Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.
* Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
* Experience carrying new design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
* Experience in MS Excel, Word, and Windows Operating Systems
* Experience with power management and power monitoring systems

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
* Knowledge of critical data center equipment
* Knowledge of engineering documentation, electrical diagrams and standard operating procedures
* Knowledge of building codes and regulations including Life Safety, BOCA, NFPA, NEC, or OSHA
* Experience in project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure
* Experience in Data Center Engineering Operations, with a deep understanding of electrical and mechanical data center infrastructure
* Experience reading and interpreting construction specifications and drawings for all domains

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.

• Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. • Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.  

* Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.
* Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
* Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.

• Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers. • Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholder’s management.  

* Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.
* Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.
* Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
* Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
* Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.
* Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
* Experience carrying new design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
* Experience in MS Excel, Word, and Windows Operating Systems
* Experience with power management and power monitoring systems

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
* Knowledge of critical data center equipment
* Knowledge of engineering documentation, electrical diagrams and standard operating procedures
* Knowledge of building codes and regulations including Life Safety, BOCA, NFPA, NEC, or OSHA
* Experience in project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure
* Experience in Data Center Engineering Operations, with a deep understanding of electrical and mechanical data center infrastructure
* Experience reading and interpreting construction specifications and drawings for all domains

**NOW HIRING: INDUSTRIAL CONTROLS & AUTOMATION ENGINEERS**

Entry-Level to Senior Electrical Engineering Opportunities

**Department:** Engineering (Electrical)

**Location:** On-site only | 531 Old Swede Road – Douglassville, PA 19518 (no remote or hybrid)

**Schedule:** Monday–Friday | 8:00AM–4:30PM | Full-time

**Compensation:** $80,000 – $120,000 annually, based on electrical/controls-programming experience, technical capability, education, ability to contribute independently, and market data

Looking for real engineering work, hands-on problem solving, and projects that actually get built?

We're looking for Electrical Engineers with strong industrial controls and automation experience, especially engineers who have programmed, commissioned, or supported automated equipment using Beckhoff Structured Text or similar IEC 61131-3 platforms.

Your controls logic, electrical designs, and troubleshooting decisions will run equipment that is built, tested, installed, and operated in real industrial environments.

You won't get lost here. Your work will be seen, and it will matter.

**No Crane Experience?** Keep Reading

Direct overhead-crane experience is valuable, but it's not the only way in. We especially want engineers from industries that design, build, integrate, or support:

* Conveyor and sortation systems
* Automated material-handling equipment
* Distribution and fulfillment centers
* Packaging and processing machinery
* Robotics and motion-control systems
* Custom industrial machinery
* Warehouse and manufacturing automation
* Systems integration
* Heavy industrial equipment

If you've designed controls for equipment that moves, positions, lifts, transfers, sequences, or automates material, your experience may translate directly to our work.

**What This Role Really Is**

This is a hands-on industrial electrical engineering and controls role focused on custom crane, hoist, motion-control, and automated material-handling systems.

You'll work across the full equipment lifecycle: electrical design, controls programming, manufacturing support, testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and field performance. Depending on experience, you'll either support projects under mentorship or own the electrical and controls scope for complex engineered systems.

This role takes more than creating drawings. Success depends on understanding how hardware, software, motors, drives, sensors, safety systems, and mechanical equipment work together as one system.

**Who Thrives Here (and Who Doesn't)**

You'll do well here if you:

* Enjoy programming and troubleshooting real industrial equipment
* Can connect controls logic to physical machine behavior
* Take ownership of technical decisions and system performance
* Are comfortable working across electrical design, software, manufacturing, and testing
* Enjoy custom-engineered projects more than repetitive product work
* Communicate well with engineers, technicians, electricians, manufacturing employees, and customers
* Want your designs to be built, tested, and used

This role is likely not a fit if you:

* Prefer software development with little interaction with physical equipment
* Want a highly segmented role limited to one narrow engineering task
* Avoid hands-on troubleshooting or manufacturing-floor involvement
* Prefer repetitive controls projects with limited customization
* Don't want accountability for how the completed system performs

**What Success Looks Like (First 90 Days)**

**Early-Career Engineers**

* Learn ACECO electrical standards, controls architecture, products, and engineering workflows
* Support electrical schematics, hardware selection, software documentation, and system testing
* Develop familiarity with PLCs, VFDs, motor controls, sensors, safety circuits, and crane operating sequences
* Build working relationships with Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing, Field Service, and Project Management
* Begin contributing to controls programming and troubleshooting under guidance

**Experienced Engineers**

* Review existing industrial-controls architecture with minimal ramp-up
* Contribute independently to Structured Text programming, electrical design, and system troubleshooting
* Begin owning the electrical and controls scope for assigned projects
* Support manufacturing and field teams during equipment testing and issue resolution
* Identify improvements to controls standards, reusable code, documentation, and workflows
* Serve as a technical resource for less experienced engineers where appropriate

**Why Join Our Team at American Crane?**

* Controls Work With Physical Impact: your software and electrical designs directly control large, highly customized industrial equipment
* Complex Automation Challenges: motors, drives, feedback devices, motion systems, safety circuits, operator interfaces, sensors, and coordinated sequences
* Transferable Experience: conveyor, warehouse automation, packaging, robotics, systems integration, and custom machinery backgrounds apply directly
* Full-System Exposure: design, programming, manufacturing support, testing, commissioning, and field troubleshooting
* Technical Ownership: engineering judgment matters here, and you'll own how your designs perform
* Stability & Growth: an established manufacturer investing in automation, connected equipment, and advanced controls

**What You'll Do**

Industrial Controls Programming

* Develop, modify, test, and troubleshoot PLC-based control systems for cranes, hoists, and material-handling equipment
* Program industrial automation applications
* Develop sequenced operations, interlocks, permissives, alarms, diagnostics, and fault-handling logic
* Support reusable programming standards, function blocks, libraries, and controls architecture
* Develop or support operator-interface and HMI functionality
* Document controls logic, software revisions, operating sequences, and system behavior

* Support system upgrades, software updates, and network security practices.

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related technical discipline.
* Minimum of five (5) years of experience in security system design, programming, or integration.
* Strong knowledge of electronic access control, CCTV, and intrusion detection systems.
* Experience with platforms such as LenelS2, Genetec, Honeywell, or Axis.
* Ability to read and interpret electrical and mechanical drawings.
* Proficiency with AutoCAD or similar design software.
* Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
* Valid driver’s license and clean driving record.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Industry certifications such as Lenel Certified Expert, Genetec Security Center, or equivalent.
* Working knowledge of IP networking, VLANs, and cybersecurity principles.
* Experience integrating security systems with BAS, fire alarm, or life safety networks.
* Familiarity with NFPA 731, UL 294, and other applicable security installation standards.
* Prior experience in a construction or building automation environment.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

* Strong technical aptitude and understanding of low-voltage systems.
* Excellent organizational, documentation, and communication skills.

Work is performed in both office and field environments. May require standing, walking, climbing ladders, and lifting up to 50 pounds during site visits or commissioning. Exposure to active construction sites and variable conditions is common. PPE is required during fieldwork.

jobs.title: Sr Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Company Overview**

**Ambiq** is on a mission to enable intelligence everywhere — powering the AI edge revolution with the world's lowest-power semiconductor solutions.

Built on our proprietary sub- and near-threshold technology, our chips deliver multi-fold improvements in energy efficiency without costly process scaling. Since 2010, we've shipped over 300 million units to customers building smarter wearables, medical devices, IoT products, and AI-powered edge applications.

Our cross-functional teams span design, research, development, production, marketing, sales, and operations across Austin, Hsinchu, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Singapore. We move fast, tackle hard problems, and create space for people to grow through complex, meaningful work that shapes the future of technology.

We're looking for self-motivated, creative problem-solvers who are eager to push technological limits and make a real impact in energy efficiency.

At Ambiq, we live by five values: **Innovate. Collaborate. Focus. Learn. Achieve.**

If that's you, join us — the intelligence everywhere revolution starts here.

**This role will be on-site 5 days a week in NW Austin.**

### **Scope**

As the Sr. Staff Software Engineer, Power Management at Ambiq, you will drive the software architecture, requirements, development, testing, and performance optimization of the SDK power management software for our latest family of low-power Edge AI MCUs. In this role, you will work closely with SoC hardware power architects, product marketing, validation, and our IP vendors to define the software architecture, functional partitioning, and requirements for the platform's power management infrastructure. You will provide technical leadership and architectural direction to the software development and system test teams, ensuring the delivery of robust, production-quality software on schedule. The role encompasses the power management infrastructure, memory control and retention, clock management, low-power operating modes, and software techniques for optimizing system-level power consumption.

The successful candidate will have extensive experience in early-stage software architecture and hands-on embedded software development. They must have a proven track record of designing, implementing, debugging, profiling, and optimizing embedded software for ARM Cortex-M processors using an RTOS. Experience developing low-level firmware, power management software, device drivers, and hardware abstraction layers is essential. The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader who enjoys solving complex technical problems while remaining actively involved in software design, implementation, code reviews, and debugging.

**Responsibilities**

* Define software requirements and functional allocations based on evolving input from SoC hardware architects, product marketing, software architects, validation and software development teams.
* Design, develop, debug, profile, and optimize the AmbiqSuite SDK power management software, including power modeling and characterization under a wide range of operating conditions.
* Own the SoC software architecture, performance, and power optimization, identifying opportunities to reduce power consumption while maintaining system performance and functionality.
* Work closely with product marketing, field engineering, validation, and system test teams to understand customer use cases and translate them into software architecture, implementation, and test requirements.
* Serve as the technical authority for power management software, reviewing software designs, architecture, code, test plans, and validation results to ensure quality, performance, and low-power operation.
* Drive cross-functional technical discussions with hardware architects, firmware developers, validation, and IP vendors to resolve architectural issues and ensure successful product execution.
* Diagnose complex system-level issues spanning hardware and software, and evaluate architectural trade-offs to achieve the optimal balance of power, performance, cost, and implementation complexity.
* Develop software for low-power operating modes, clock management, memory retention, wake-up sequencing, and other power management infrastructure components.
* Define and implement methodologies, tools, and metrics for measuring, profiling, and optimizing software power consumption.
* Work with relevant teams to ensure power-optimized implementation of the RTOS ports for Ambiq SoCs.
* Provide technical leadership through design reviews, code reviews, technical mentoring, and by establishing software development best practices.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
* 10+ years of experience developing embedded software for ARM Cortex-M–based systems in bare-metal and RTOS environments.
* Expert-level C/C++ programming skills, with experience developing low-level firmware, device drivers, hardware abstraction layers (HAL), and startup code. Experience with ARM assembly language is a plus.
* Strong understanding of SoC architecture, including processor subsystems, memory hierarchy, bus interconnects, interrupts, DMA engines, cache architectures, memory protection, inter-processor communication, and shared memory systems.
* Proven experience designing, implementing, debugging, profiling, and optimizing software for ultra-low-power embedded systems.
* Strong understanding of embedded power management techniques, including clock management, voltage and frequency scaling, power domains, memory retention, clock gating, and low-power operating modes.
* Experience profiling and analyzing power consumption across software and hardware boundaries, including identifying and resolving system-level performance and power bottlenecks.
* Hands-on experience using embedded development and debug tools, including JTAG/SWD debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power analyzers

jobs.description:
**Standard Job Description**
----------------------------

You will be an Algorithm Engineer on the Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Sensor Fusion team, working at the forefront of sensor fusion, perception, and autonomy for fighter and unmanned platforms. In this role you will have a significant impact on shaping the future of Sensor Fusion across Aeronautics, defining the vision for our next‑generation platforms, and integrating Lockheed Martin’s most advanced technologies. If you thrive on pushing the envelope, enjoy tackling difficult algorithmic challenges, and are passionate about turning novel sensor concepts into flight‑ready software, this position on our Emerging‑Technology Sensor Fusion team is for you.

As an engineer working in sensor fusion you will possess a combination of skills from various disciplines:

**Programming Fundamentals**

Programming Languages: Proficiency in languages such as Python, C++, C#, or MATLAB.  
Software Frameworks: Familiarity with software frameworks, such as NumPy, SciPy, or TensorFlow, MATLAB, MATLAB Object Oriented, for numerical computations.  
Simulation Tools: Knowledge of simulation tools, such as Simulink or MATLAB, for modeling and testing sensor fusion systems.

**Mathematical Foundations**

Linear Algebra: Understanding of vector spaces, linear transformations, and matrix operations.  
Probability Theory and Statistics: Familiarity with probability distributions, Bayes' theorem, and stochastic processes. Knowledge of statistical inference, estimation, and hypothesis testing.  
Advanced topics: Understanding of numerical optimization, convex optimization, non-linear optimization, machine learning, and/or mathematical methods.

**Signal Processing and Filtering**

Signal Processing: Understanding of signal processing techniques, such as filtering, convolution, and Fourier analysis.  
Kalman Filter: Familiarity with the Kalman filter algorithm, its variants (e.g., Extended Kalman Filter, Unscented Kalman Filter), and applications.  
Particle Filter: Knowledge of particle filter algorithms and their applications in non-linear, non-Gaussian systems.

**Tracking**

Embedded Development: Acute proficiency in Programming Fundamentals applied to embedded systems.  
Sensor Modeling: Understanding of sensor characteristics, noise models, calibration techniques, Signal Processing and Filtering, and Mathematical Foundations.  
Data Association: Familiarity with data association techniques, such as nearest neighbor, joint probabilistic data association, and multiple hypothesis tracking.  
State Estimation: Knowledge of state estimation algorithms, including Kalman filters, particle filters, and Bayesian estimation methods.

**Sensor Integration and Management**

Resource Allocation: Experience tasking, prioritizing, and scheduling of sensors and maximizing information value, system needs, or target tracking accuracy with a deep understanding of Programming Fundamentals.  
Sensor Integration: Experience with integrating sensors like LIDAR, RADAR, or cameras and offboard sources.

**Basic Qualifications**
------------------------

- Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a related field

- Experience with C++, C#, Rust, MATLAB, and/or Python

- Real Time Operating System (RTOS) experience – (Windows & Linux)

- Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills to work effectively with cross-functional teams

**Desired Skills**
------------------

- Project experience in sensor fusion sub-domain(s) (e.g. state estimation, identification, correlation, sensor tasking) or coursework across domains including signal processing, artificial intelligence, autonomy/perception, artificial intelligence, navigation, or control systems in a sensor/systems application.

- Experience implementing Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or statistical algorithms in real time operating systems

- Strong understanding of Object Oriented Programming (OOP)/Object Oriented Design (OOD)

- Strong mathematical foundation in Linear Algebra, Probability Theory, and Statistics

**Pay Information**

Full-Time Salary Range: $67000.00 - $124400.00

jobs.title: Senior Electrical and Controls Engineer
jobs.description:
At Compu Dynamics, we don't just build infrastructure—we create the backbone of the digital future. As North America's premier technology infrastructure design-build partner, we design, construct, and maintain mission-critical data centers for some of the world's most innovative companies. With roots in one of the fastest-growing data center markets in the world, our growth is as intentional as our impact.

**About Compu Dynamics Modular**

Compu Dynamics Modular (CDM) is at the forefront of innovative modular solutions, specializing in Modular Data Centers (MDC), metal frame systems, and fully integrated enclosures. Our designs are scalable, efficient, and sustainable, tailored to meet the evolving needs of our clients in a dynamic industry.

  

**Summary/Objective:**

The **Senior Electrical and Controls Engineer** is a technical leader responsible for driving the design, development, and implementation of electrical and control systems across Compu Dynamics Modular's data center and commercial modular products. This role provides expertise from early-stage concepting through manufacturing, installation, and site commissioning. The Senior Electrical and Controls Engineer is a key contributor to product innovation and standardization and serves as a mentor to junior engineers, modular designers, and project managers .

  

This individual is recognized as a subject matter expert within the company and plays a critical role in maintaining compliance with all codes, improving processes, and delivering cutting-edge modular infrastructure solutions.

  

**Essential Functions:**

**1. Electrical Design & Engineering Leadership**

* Lead the electrical and controls system design process for modular product development, including commercial and data center applications.
* Develop and review one-line diagrams, electrical schematics, cable schedules, load lists, and detailed designs using AutoCAD
* Calculate electrical loads, select equipment, and perform code analysis to ensure design compliance.
* Generate complete electrical Bills of Material
* Collaborate with manufacturing teams to ensure designs meet production best practices and are constructible.
* Develop PLC and HMI based environmental monitoring systems from a hardware and software perspective
* Select monitoring systems and instruments as required, including biometric access, alarming systems, fire detection systems, leak detection, temperature, pressure, and humidity sensors

**2. Project & Product Development Support**

* Guide electrical scope development during bids and conceptual design phases; assist in cost estimation and proposal generation.
* Review and approve submittals, RFIs, and shop drawings; provide technical documentation and responses to client or inspector inquiries.
* Support field activities including site surveys, system troubleshooting, and commissioning support.
* Generate required installation and maintenance documentation

**3. Cross-functional Collaboration & Vendor Coordination**

* Interface with clients, contractors, and internal stakeholders to resolve design issues and clarify technical requirements.
* Coordinate vendor selections based on technical and performance requirements; manage relationships with manufacturer representatives.
* Review external control schematics and ensure alignment with modular system needs.

**4. Compliance & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead efforts to ensure compliance with NEC, local codes, safety regulations, and internal documentation standards.
* Develop and maintain internal electrical design standards, tools, and templates.
* Research and implement industry best practices for modular system design and integration.

**5. Mentorship & Technical Leadership**

* Provide training and guidance to junior engineers and modular design staff.
* Conduct peer reviews and technical audits across project teams.
* Contribute to long-term engineering strategy and process improvement initiatives.

  

**Competencies:**

* Deep knowledge of electrical power systems, controls, and modular design.

* Proficiency in AutoCAD, Revit and Microsoft Office Suite.

* Familiarity with controller software (e.g., PLC and HMI based systems)

* Fundamental understanding of industrial networking protocols and BMS interface

* Excellent communication and technical writing skills.

* Strong analytical and creative problem-solving abilities.

* Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple concurrent projects.

**Supervisory Responsibility:**

This role may mentor and oversee work performed by junior engineers or modular designers but does not have formal direct reports.

**Work Environment:**

Work is primarily performed in an office or collaborative environment with occasional site visits. Field work may include exposure to active construction, elevated temperatures, and energized equipment.

  

**Physical Demands:**

Must be able to conduct site walks, climb ladders, and lift up to 25 pounds occasionally. Must be comfortable working in manufacturing and job site environments when necessary.

**Position Type:**

Full-time, non-exempt. Work hours follow the service department schedule and may include occasional overtime.

**Travel:**

Up to 15% travel may be required for site walks, commissioning support, or vendor meetings.

**Required Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or similar field.
* 10+ years of experience in electrical engineering with an emphasis on commercial, industrial, or mission-critical projects.
* Expert-level understanding of power distribution, control systems, and electrical code compliance.

**Preferred Education and Experience:**

* Professional Engineering (PE) license strongly preferred.
* Certifications such as LEED, CEM, or CPD are a plus.
* Modular construction or data center infrastructure design experience.

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.

• Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. • Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.  

* Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.
* Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.
* Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.

• Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers. • Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholder’s management.  

* Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.
* Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.
* Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
* Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
* Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.
* Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
* Experience carrying new design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
* Experience in MS Excel, Word, and Windows Operating Systems
* Experience with power management and power monitoring systems

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
* Knowledge of critical data center equipment
* Knowledge of engineering documentation, electrical diagrams and standard operating procedures
* Knowledge of building codes and regulations including Life Safety, BOCA, NFPA, NEC, or OSHA
* Experience in project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure
* Experience in Data Center Engineering Operations, with a deep understanding of electrical and mechanical data center infrastructure
* Experience reading and interpreting construction specifications and drawings for all domains

You'll develop software running on embedded Linux platforms, solve complex multithreading and interprocess communication challenges, optimize system-level performance, and troubleshoot integration issues across software, operating systems, and physical hardware.

jobs.title: Senior Instrumentation & Controls Engineer - Hardware
jobs.description:
**About Valar Atomics**

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

**The Team**

You will be joining Valar Atomics' I&C and Controls Engineering team within the Fuel Manufacturing group. I&C Hardware Engineers own the physical measurement and control layer field instrumentation and final elements, control panels and I/O architecture, field wiring and network infrastructure, and safety instrumented system hardware. You will work alongside I&C Software, process, electrical, mechanical, and nuclear safety engineers in a hands-on environment where measurement quality and installation integrity directly support production reliability and nuclear safety. The team values technical depth, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

**The Role**

Valar Atomics is seeking an I&C Hardware Engineer to specify, design, install, commission, and maintain the instrumentation and control hardware for nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. The role covers field instrument and final element selection, control panel and I/O architecture design, hazardous area classification, safety instrumented system hardware, field wiring and network infrastructure, calibration, loop commissioning, and control loop tuning supporting both capital projects and ongoing plant operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Select, size, and specify field instrumentation including flow, pressure, differential pressure, temperature, level, and analytical devices; produce instrument data sheets, specifications, and requisitions.
* Size and specify final control elements including control valves, actuators, positioners, regulators, on-off valves, and flow elements; perform valve sizing, noise and cavitation checks, and actuator thrust verification.
* Design control panels and remote I/O architecture including enclosure layout and rating, I/O module and channel allocation, terminal and marshalling arrangement, power distribution, UPS sizing, isolators, and intrinsic safety barriers.
* Perform hazardous area classification and select equipment for classified areas in accordance with NEC Article 500/505 or IEC 60079; prepare intrinsic safety loop calculations and verify entity parameters.
* Develop and maintain instrumentation engineering documentation including the instrument index, loop diagrams, hook-up drawings, I/O lists, instrument location plans, cable schedules, and P&ID instrumentation mark-ups.
* Support safety instrumented system hardware scope including SIL determination input, safety sensor and final element selection, redundancy and voting architecture, proof test interval and procedure development, and SIL verification calculations in accordance with IEC 61511 and IEC 61508.
* Tune PID and advanced regulatory control loops; commission field instrumentation; diagnose and resolve loop deviations, valve response problems, and measurement quality issues.
* Establish and execute the instrument calibration program including calibration procedures, ranges, tolerances, traceability to NIST-referenced standards, calibration records, and recall scheduling.
* Specify and oversee installation of field wiring and physical OT network infrastructure including cable schedules, tray and conduit routing, media selection, signal and power segregation, grounding and shielding practice, and field switch and cabinet placement.
* Prepare and execute hardware FAT, SAT, and commissioning plans; perform point-to-point continuity checks, loop checks, calibration verification, and end-to-end interlock testing from sensor through final element; produce turnover and as-built documentation.
* Diagnose and resolve field faults including I/O channel failures, transmitter drift, positioner and actuator faults, and wiring, grounding, or noise-induced signal problems; perform root cause analysis and document corrective actions.
* Support instrument reliability engineering including criticality and spares analysis, failure rate data collection, preventive and predictive maintenance strategy, and obsolescence planning.
